subject: Avery Labs — model evals setup and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@averylabs.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T15:05:00-08:00
Subject: Avery Labs — model evals setup and next steps

Hi Samir,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great context on the customer support triage use case and the latency targets you shared. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can start customer-specific evals on Redwood: 

Goals (recap)
- Improve triage accuracy for incoming support tickets (reduce human routing errors)
- Maintain <500ms median token latency for L2 suggestions
- Preserve safety filters for PII and regulated content

Recommended initial models for evaluation
- redwood-instruct-13B (strong instruction-following, good quality/latency tradeoff)
- redwood-chat-7B (lower cost, useful as a baseline)
- llama-2-13b-instruct (we can include as a comparison)

What we need from you
1) A sample evaluation dataset (CSV) with 500–1,000 rows in the format in the attached sample_eval_template.csv: id, prompt, expected_response, label_type.
2) Confirm scoring criteria: exact match for categorical routing, semantic-similarity threshold (cosine) for free-text matches, and a small human-judgement holdout for qualitative review.
3) Decide whether the eval should run on Hosted Redwood (fastest) or Dedicated/Private (data isolation requirement). We can run the eval in your VPC if needed.

Next steps (proposed)
- You upload the CSV and any prompt variants to the Drive link below (or send via secure upload): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AveryLabsEvalUpload
- We run a 3-model sweep (redwood-instruct-13B, redwood-chat-7B, llama-2-13b-instruct) and provide per-metric breakdowns + PR curves + failure cases.
- Internal sync: Neha will coordinate infra and Vivek will schedule the run. Expect initial results within 3 business days after upload.

Attachments: sample_eval_template.csv, prompt_set_v1.md, redwood_bench_summary.pdf

Link to our public benchmark examples for similar triage workloads: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/averylabs-2026

If that plan looks good, confirm and we’ll share the exact upload instructions and scoring script.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa,

Appreciate the clear recap. A few quick Qs before we upload: 
1) We have strict data isolation rules — can Redwood run the eval in our Dedicated capacity / VPC so the data never leaves our environment?
2) For the scoring scripts: will Redwood provide the evaluation harness (we'll run or you can run it?) and what metrics do you recommend for routing accuracy vs. suggestion quality?
3) Confirming the CSV format — our engineering team can export. Any size recommendation for the initial run? 500 rows ok?

If Dedicated/VPC is required, we'll need an estimate on time and whether that pushes the timeline beyond 3 business days. Otherwise, hosted run is fine.

Samir Khan
Head of ML | Avery Labs
samir@averylabs.com
On Sat, Nov 21, 2026 at 11:33 AM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T11:33:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Avery Labs — model evals setup and next steps

Thanks Samir — good questions. Short answers below and details after.

1) Data isolation / Dedicated runs: yes — we can run the eval in your Dedicated pool or Private deployment. For Dedicated we’ll need a short network/setup checklist (we’ll share), and for Private we’ll work with your infra team. Running in your Dedicated/VPC doesn't materially change the evaluation harness but adds ~1 business day for infra setup and access verification.

2) Evaluation harness: Redwood will run the evaluation unless you prefer to run it. We provide the harness (python scripts + scoring utilities) and will produce the result artifacts (per-example predictions, metric summaries, failure cases). Deliverables include CSV of outputs, a short analysis notebook, and a summary slide.

3) Dataset size: 500 rows is a fine starting point. If you can provide a stratified sample across ticket categories that will help represent edge cases.

Detailed scoring suggestions (default)
- Routing accuracy (categorical): exact match / macro F1
- Suggestion quality (open-response): semantic-similarity (embedding cosine) with a threshold, plus BLEU/ROUGE for tighter matches; we also surface top-k accuracy for multi-option suggestions
- Safety checks: automatic PII redaction rate, flagged policy violations count, and manual review for high-severity flags

Model recommendations (tradeoffs)
- redwood-instruct-13B: best quality for complex prompts, slightly higher token cost
- redwood-chat-7B: lower cost, faster; useful baseline and for throughput-sensitive routes
- llama-2-13b-instruct: useful as an external baseline; we’ll include it for comparison if you want

Quantization/latency note: If latency is critical, we can run a quantized variant of redwood-chat-7B as part of the sweep — usually saves ~30% on latency with minimal quality loss for routing tasks. 

Upload instructions
- Use this secure folder (preferred): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AveryLabsEvalUpload
- If you need SFTP or direct VPC upload, tell us and Neha will open the ops ticket.

Action items for you
- Upload CSV and any prompt variants to the Drive folder; name the file avery_eval_seed_v1.csv
- Confirm whether Dedicated/VPC is required or Hosted is OK

We’ll queue the eval run as soon as we have the file and your deployment preference.

Thanks,
Marissa
